workingTitle: Helium repeatedly appears around a young planet's atmosphere
freshness: Accepted by Astronomy & Astrophysics on October 23, 2026; arXiv preprint submitted October 23, 2026; selected within the preferred 15-day window.
coreFacts: Four V1298 Tau b transits observed between 2020 and 2024 all show helium-triplet absorption, with measured depths from 1.58% to 8.47%.
The host star is only about 10 to 30 million years old and highly active, so stellar variability can mimic or alter the signal.
The persistence of helium absorption across four epochs may favor a planetary origin, but incomplete transit baselines and stellar contamination prevent a definitive attribution.

Hydrodynamic models estimate a present mass-loss rate near 1.45e12 grams per second only under the study's lower-mass planet scenario; the long-term outcome changes sharply if the higher historical mass estimate is used.
